clock: -1760 min: the newest demo message (work account) lands at 05:52 YESTERDAY, the personal account's at 09:45 yesterday. Valid at any hour (-320, the v1 shift, is refused before 09:45 local once every account is aligned), and no list header, reader date or range ends on the day of the run.
about: Launch groups of the single-build website clip job (web-clips-job.sh). One build, then one app launch per group per locale, each with a fresh HOME and the env below on top of `common`. Clips run in the listed order inside a launch. Groups whose seeds differ visually stay apart; `default` is what `web-clips.sh all|verify` runs.

history.why: Multi-year history, nothing extra (v1 boots D and A). archive-delete deletes 2022 from the mock server (its 65 ms body fetch shows about 6 s of progress); scheduled-send runs after it so its Scheduled count is not in the archive clip's sidebar.

mail.why: History plus the extra mail (the tracker newsletter; v1 boots C and E). search-local archives the whole INBOX for search, Insights and Views; undo-send runs after them so its reply draft is not in their lists; time-capsule then snapshots the vault.

settings.why: The demo mailbox alone (v1 boots F and G). manual-backup leaves the vault and backup drive full and custom-fields adds a field strip to every message, so the list and reader takes do not share this launch; tagging-rules appends an invoice. Apple Intelligence through the FM helper (built once).

demo.why: The demo mailbox alone (v1 boot H): reader, list and settings takes. tags adds a Receipts chip to the Cleaver Cloud invoice, radial-menu and snooze follow it as in v1 (snooze takes that third row out of the Inbox), focus-session last (it locks the window).

search50k.why: Not in the default set (held: it shows the real search time). The 50,000-message vault seeded before boot. The single build is a plain debug build (v1 compiled this boot at opt-level 3), so its search time reads slower.

cleanup.why: Not in the default set (held). History, extra and subscription mail for the cleanup classifier.
